subject: Regional egress windows, pinning guarantees and subprocessor schedule
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clearhealth.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: security@clearhealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Initial ask: Can Redwood commit to EU-region-only processing with transient analytics hop window?

Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — ClearHealth is excited about the performance profile. Before we move to procurement, our legal and security teams need written clarity on a couple of points:

- Can Redwood commit to processing customer traffic and derived artifacts for our tenant in the EU (region pinning) excluding transient analytics hops? If not, what are the documented windows for temporary egress (minutes/hours/days)?
- We need the current subprocessor roster and a cadence for updates. Any plans to add third-party analytics or logging vendors in the next 90 days?
- If there are cross-border hops for tooling (metrics/alerts), what controls—KMS, transient logs, or encryption—are in place?

Can you share a proposed DPA addendum or statement we can include in our security questionnaire? We need something we can circulate internally by EOD Friday.

Appreciate it,

Elena Ruiz
Head of Security Programs
ClearHealth

Attachment: security_questionnaire_20261124.xlsx (reference)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clearhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: Can Redwood commit to EU-region-only processing with transient analytics hop window?

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes, we support EU region pinning for customer compute and persistent artifacts; we also have a documented transient analytics "egress window" policy for telemetry that we can narrow for enterprise contracts.

Details and artifacts attached: a draft DPA addendum tailored to region pinning and a CSV of the current subprocessor roster. Highlights:
- Region pinning: We can bind the tenant to eu-west-1 for processing and storage. This includes model inference, embeddings, and persisted logs.
- Transient analytics hop: By default we allow a 30-minute ephemeral routing window for internal metrics to cross to central metrics services (for aggregation). For cleared enterprise customers we can contractually reduce this to a 5-minute window or remove it entirely by enabling a private metrics sink.
- Cross-border tooling controls: Telemetry in the transient window is always encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and keys are customer-isolated for Private deployments (KMS integration). For hosted tenants we use envelope encryption; keys for EU-pinned tenants can be escrowed in a customer KMIP/KMS.

Attachments (2): clearhealth_dpa_addendum_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster_nov2026.csv

Proposed next steps: 1) Review the draft addendum, 2) If acceptable, we can provide a DocuSign link for the addendum + DPA schedule, 3) We can schedule a 30-min technical call to walk the security team through transient metrics architecture.

I cc'd Rishi (legal) and Marissa (privacy) to help with any contract language.

Best,

---
Monica Patel
Sr. Manager, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
Attachment: clearhealth_dpa_addendum_v1.pdf (2 pages)
Attachment: subprocessor_roster_nov2026.csv (roster)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:24:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Proposed DPA wording + compromise on egress window

Folks — forwarding Monica's draft and flagging a couple contract edits I recommend before we send the DocuSign:

1) Egress window clause: modify "30-minute default" language to specify measurement boundaries (start = first packet to non-EU telemetry endpoint; end = final aggregated metric receipt) and allow customers to require either a max 5-minute window OR host a private metrics sink (we should make the latter explicit).
2) Subprocessor updates: commit to 30-day advance notice for roster changes with an "opt-out" clause for high-sensitivity customers (they can require explicit written consent for any new non-EU subprocessor).
3) Audit evidence: offer to provide a rolling 90-day export of transient egress logs for the tenant (redacted) on request as part of the compliance package.

Marissa/Soojin — can you confirm whether the data retention language in section 4.2 aligns with the EU consumer privacy baseline? If not, I'll propose alternate text.

Rishi
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Monica / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick follow-ups. A few clarifying asks from Legal / InfoSec:
- We appreciate the 5-minute contractable window. Can you confirm whether that 5-minute window is inclusive of retries and async aggregation? If retries can extend the observable window, we need the contractual cap to account for that.
- For the 30-day advanced notice of subprocessor changes — will that notice include the planned geolocation of the new subprocessor (i.e., whether they will process data outside the EU)?
- Please confirm the format and delivery mechanism for the rolling 90-day egress log export (S3 CSV or a secure Drive link). We prefer S3 with customer-side encryption if possible.

We need a signed addendum before procurement will route to finance; is DocuSign availability possible today?

Best,

Elena

> On Thu, 26 Nov 2026 at 11:24 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clearhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Regional egress windows, pinning guarantees and subprocessor schedule

Elena —

Great questions. Answers below and next steps at the bottom.

1) 5-minute window and retries: The 5-minute contractual cap will be defined as "time between initial telemetry emission and final write to aggregated metrics storage, inclusive of automatic retry attempts initiated by Redwood's ingestion pipeline but exclusive of manual replay actions by operators." In practice our pipeline retries are backoffs with a capped retry TTL of 30s per attempt and a max of 3 attempts, so the contract language will note retries are included in the 5-minute SLA and that manual intervention is explicitly excluded.

2) Subprocessor notice: Yes — the 30-day notice will include the planned processing region(s) for the new subprocessor and a short risk summary. For high-sensitivity customers like ClearHealth we can add a clause requiring explicit written consent prior to onboarding any subprocessor that will process EU-pinned traffic outside the EU.

3) Rolling 90-day export: We can deliver the rolling export as an encrypted S3 bucket (customer-managed SSE-C or KMS) with an agreed prefix and lifecycle. Delivery will be via pre-signed HTTPS URLs we rotate daily.

DocuSign: we can produce a pre-filled addendum and route today — we will send a DocuSign link to your security@clearhealth.com address if you confirm signatory name and title (we assume Procurement signs on behalf of ClearHealth).

Next steps (proposed):
- Rishi to finalize two minor language edits (see prior email) — target EOD today.
- Monica to send DocuSign link once legal signs off.
- Technical 30-min call to demo private metrics sink option (if desired) — I can host tomorrow.

If that plan works, I'll queue the DocuSign now and mark the addendum as an "EU-pin + transient telemetry" addendum.

Thanks,

--
Monica Patel
Sr. Manager, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
